skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Edit existing video on RunComfy — this skill is a smart router that matches the user's intent to the right edit model in the RunComfy catalog. Picks Wan 2.7 Edit-Video (general restyle / background swap / packaging swap, identity + motion preservation), Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control (transfer precise motion from a reference video to a target character), or Lucy Edit Restyle (lightweight identity-stable restyle / outfit swap). Bundles each model's documented prompting patterns so the skill gets sharper edits without burning iterations on the wrong model. Calls `runcomfy run <vendor>/<model>/<endpoint>` through the local RunComfy CLI. Triggers on "video edit", "edit video", "restyle video", "swap video background", "motion control", "outfit swap video", or any explicit ask to transform a video.
skill.summary: Route video edits to suitable RunComfy models for restyling, motion transfer, background changes, and outfit swaps.
skill.author: genmedia-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder HTTPS URLs, and ellipses misread as path traversal. Confirmed risks include unpinned third-party installation, external CLI execution, unsafe shell interpolation of user-derived JSON, and disclosed third-party processing of prompts and media.

remediation.issue: User-derived text is embedded in shell commands as inline JSON.
remediation.suggestion: Pass arguments through a structured process API or a protected JSON input file. Never concatenate prompts or URLs into a shell command string.

remediation.issue: Installation commands use mutable, unversioned npm and GitHub sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer, CLI package, and skill source to reviewed versions or immutable commits. Publish integrity hashes for downloaded artifacts.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media URLs are processed by a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before submitting sensitive content. Document provider retention, access, deletion, and media URL exposure policies.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Injection Risk in Inline JSON Commands
semantic_findings.description: Examples place prompts and media URLs inside single-quoted JSON passed through a shell. Line 222 considers only CLI expansion, but shell parsing occurs before the CLI receives the argument.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill is designed to insert user edit text into these commands, and the examples rely on shell quoting. One example manually escapes an apostrophe, but no general escaping requirement is defined.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party Code Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup runs an unversioned npx tool against a mutable repository and globally installs the latest RunComfy CLI. A compromised future release could execute during installation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both commands visibly omit immutable versions or commit references. npm and npx installation can execute package lifecycle code.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Processing of Prompts and Media
semantic_findings.description: The CLI sends prompts to RunComfy, directs its servers to fetch supplied media URLs, and downloads generated results. Sensitive prompts or media leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The networking and third-party fetch behavior is explicitly documented. This is expected functionality, but it creates a clear privacy boundary.

content.user_title: Edit Videos with Intent-Routed AI Models
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong video model wastes time and weakens identity or motion consistency. This skill routes each edit to a suitable RunComfy model with focused prompts.
actual_capabilities: Routes general restyles, background swaps, and packaging changes to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video.
Routes reference-driven character motion transfer to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control.
Routes lightweight outfit, lighting, and scene restyles to Lucy Edit Restyle.
Builds model-specific prompts that prioritize identity, motion, framing, or audio preservation.
Supports reference images, source videos, resolution settings, duration limits, and output directories where each model permits them.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access.
Sends prompts and media locations to RunComfy for remote processing.
Uses one model per request and does not blend routes.
Outputs remain subject to model limits, including duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and input size.

use_cases.title: Polish Product Videos
use_cases.description: Replace packaging or backgrounds while preserving framing, hand movement, camera motion, and source audio.

use_cases.title: Transfer Character Motion
use_cases.description: Map movement from a reference clip onto a target character while maintaining visual identity.

use_cases.title: Restyle Short Social Clips
use_cases.description: Change outfits, lighting, or atmosphere while preserving faces, poses, and motion.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit {video_url}. Preserve the subject's face, pose, motion, and audio. Change only the background to {background_description}.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Packaging Swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use {reference_image_url} to replace the package design in {video_url}. Preserve framing, hand movement, camera motion, and original audio.

prompt_templates.title: Character Motion Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer motion from {motion_video_url} to the character in {character_image_url}. Keep the character identity and {sound_preference}.

prompt_templates.title: Constrained Restyle
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle {video_url} with {single_visual_change}. Preserve {identity_features}, {motion_features}, framing, and aspect ratio. Use {resolution} and seed {seed}.

output_examples.input: Replace a talking-head background with a neutral office and keep the speaker unchanged.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7 Edit-Video. The edit preserves face, pose, lip movement, framing, and original audio while changing only the background.

output_examples.input: Make the target character follow the dance from a reference clip.
output_examples.output: Selected Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control. The target image defines character identity, while the reference video supplies motion and optional sound.

output_examples.input: Change a walking subject's outfit to business attire without changing their face.
output_examples.output: Selected Lucy Edit Restyle. The prompt limits the change to clothing and preserves the subject's face and motion at 720p.

best_practices: State preservation requirements before the requested visual change.
Request one edit direction per run to reduce temporal drift.
Use reference media only when a specific appearance or motion must transfer.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated outfit, background, lighting, and character changes in one request.
Do not send confidential media without approval for third-party processing.
Do not interpolate untrusted prompts or URLs directly into shell command strings.

faq.question: Which model handles general video edits?
faq.answer: Wan 2.7 Edit-Video is the default for restyling, background changes, packaging swaps, and commercial polish.

faq.question: Which model transfers motion from another video?
faq.answer: Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control maps motion from a reference clip onto a target character.

faq.question: Which model is suitable for outfit swaps?
faq.answer: Lucy Edit Restyle handles localized outfit, lighting, and atmospheric changes with identity preservation.

faq.question: Can the skill preserve source audio?
faq.answer: Wan supports original audio, and Kling can retain reference sound. Available audio controls depend on the selected route.

faq.question: Does processing occur locally?
faq.answer: No. The local CLI submits jobs to RunComfy, where prompts and referenced media are processed remotely.

faq.question: What output limits apply?
faq.answer: Wan supports short clips up to 1080p, Kling supports route-dependent durations, and Lucy is limited to 720p without aspect control.
